notes_summary: Early PLG lead. Indie dev duo (founder + 1). Signed up via GitHub template and used free credits to prototype a lightweight code assistant extension for a niche editor. Wants low-latency completions inside IDE, cheap per-token cost, ability to pin model versions later. No AE contact yet — inbound only.
detailed_notes:
- Founders: Maya Patel (founder/engineer) + Jonah Reyes (cofounder/product)
- Use-case: in-editor code completions + quick summarization of PRs and docs; short-form generation, inline code explanations.
- Workload expected: bursts of low-latency chat/completion traffic tied to active dev sessions; mostly short prompts (20-120 tokens).
- Latency target: median < 150ms for single-token step; end-to-end completion < 800ms typical.
- Throughput: small concurrency (1-10 concurrent devs at MVP), scale to 50-100 as they grow.
- Cost sensitivity: high. Founders indicated they are comfortable with free tier + low-cost paid plan; will re-evaluate after $200/mo.
- Model preferences: open to smaller local/quantized variants for cost, but wants Redwood-curated models with consistent latency. Mentioned preference for gpt-style open models for licensing reasons.
- Routing/fallback: wants automatic fallback to cheaper model during spikes.
- Security/compliance: storing minimal snippets, but concerned about audit logs and token-level billing. Asked about data retention and ability to delete logs via API.
- Quote from Maya (signup call): "We want something that doesn't flicker in the editor — low latency or it's unusable. Also can't blow the bank while we test."
